Your Training

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-your-training-6431205




Summary of practice

1. Listen to the Entitlement lesson audio. You may want to listen more than once.

2. Write out your attachments. What are you attached to? What do you feel is yours?
What do you feel you deserve or are owed? How do you suffer, or will suffer emotionally
when these things don’t behave, or act in the way you wish?

3. Key word to notice are: My, mine, own, owed, deserve, have etc.



Some notes

The princesses agreements with the creator, whatever you envision Her to be, are part of
your entitlement agreements. Your princess feels that there is a contract. And your
princess wants God, or Life, to uphold and deliver the other end of the contract. You
probably feel you deserve what your imagined bargained contract says you deserve.
However, you will see that you just made that agreement with a different part of your
imagination. You called that external part God, or creator, etc. However, it was just with
your own mind.

Everything that ever lives will also die. After you are over the shock, sadness, grief, and
horror of this, you can build a new belief based in reality.

So what will you do with yourself with the time that you have?

I want to encourage you to treat yourself well. Respect your self, love your self, and don’t
let anyone mistreat you.

However where this attitude and self respect can become self destructive is when the
Princess Archetype creates expectations of entitlement about it.

In the raw world without interpretation or agreement there is no such thing as “fair” or
“entitlements” or “deserving.” By the same token there is no such constructs of “not
deserving”, “unfair”, or “not entitled”. These concepts are only the symbols that mask our
personal beliefs. Unravel these personal beliefs and you can recover your personal power
back from the victim archetype as well.

My body is just on loan to me for a while. At any moment it will go back to the earth as
dust and ashes.


                                                                                                               1/2

This session outlines some details on the Princess Archetype and how it can corrupt good
intentions into expectations and emotional attachments. This leads to emotional
suffering.

Being quick to identify the key words that the Princess uses will help you to see the
attitude earlier and get you free of the emotional traps.

Do your best to treat your self well, but that doesn’t mean that you are somehow owed or
entitled anything. The more your feel deserving, the less gratitude you will feel in your
life.

unknown thing that could take them away in a moment.

If you are aware of this, then you will appreciate them and enjoy them even more while
you have them, but not be attached or suffer when they are gone.

I hope you enjoy all the things in your life til you are long past 100 years old. And that you
lovingly let them go before your last breath.

And, in all the days before then you never fear losing them. That is easiest to do if you are
completely aware that they are all temporarily on loan to you from this world.

Obstacles you are likely to find

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-obstacles-you-are-likely-to-find-6431206

Many illusions are shattered in this lesson. These illusions make us comfortable, but they
aren’t the truth. When reality breaks these illusions that uncomfortable feeling returns,
but is now exaggerated with feelings of injustice and unfairness. I’m inviting you in this
exercise to face some obvious realities. You don’t control that body, your breath, pain,
illness, or death, for yourself, or anyone else.

You don’t control the electricity, hot and cold running water, or the weather, traffic, and
how tall you are. You don’t control whether people are nice to you or rude. They have their
lives to deal work through and they might be unconscious and feel you are just in their
way.

This can be humbling. Humbling is another word for the ego collapsing. In this case, it is
specifically the princess part of the ego.

This humility requires you drop illusions about what you control. It also allows you to
appreciate all that you have as a gift.

I am sure this is all very comforting in a truthful obvious way. The kind of way that allows
your consciousness and soul to relax. However, all the beliefs that have emotional
attachments… yeah,,,, they might scream in protest.

Lesson Transcript

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-lesson-transcript-6588380

Hello there this is Gary van Warmerdam with the audio series from pathway to happiness.
Today’s topic is about the facts of life. We could also say it’s about the facts of life and
death. It’s about entitlement, specifically about entitlement and expectations. It’s about
entitlement and expectation because that’s one of the mechanisms in the mind where we
create attachments and through those attachments we create suffering, great emotional
suffering and unhappiness and is kind of simple as a concept to say oh I got it. It’s entirely
a different thing to do about issues you find important in your life or circumstances that
you are passionate about.

The reason I share this specific slice of the one of the mechanisms in the mind that create
suffering is so that you can use this insight, this awareness to step out of it, to step out of
this unhappiness, make your peace with the world and be happier. I do not share this
because you should give up on things or say the attachment to having something. That is
not what I’m asking you to do. I’m asking you to recognize where in life it’s time to detach
and how to remain engaged in life and passionate about something while detached from
the outcome of it.

We are working on a series about creating the life that you want. The danger in that is
becoming so attached to it that you make yourself unhappy because it isn’t there fast
enough it, isn’t there soon enough, it isn’t showing up the way you intended and this is
that little trick in the mind that create suffering while we are busy consciously creating
and it’s an artful balance between the two, this conscious creation aspect of life, what we
intend and what we create, without expecting it, without being attached to it.

There’s very clear distinctions between intending and creating something and expecting it
which is to cling to the picture of it in your mind, to hope for it, to feel that it should
happened, expected, feel entitled. Those are very different things than expressing the
creation of it. The differences between intent and expectation. Intent is an opportunity to
create, expectation is an opportunity for suffering. And I cover this in some stories.

Consider for a moment that you have a business. Let’s say you have a bookstore and it’s a
wonderful little bookstore and it’s a great little dream of your life and the shopping center
is planned across the street and Barnes & Noble, big bookseller moves in across the street.
For those of you in other countries who don’t know what Barnes & Noble is, it’s a big
bookstore chain and it takes away your business and you go out of business. Did they steal
your dream, did they destroy your business?

Let’s just say as the food chain in the business world, of the big fish eating the little fish. Is
it an injustice? Depends on your point of view. From the point of view of the investors, the
owners, the people who work at Barnes & Noble, no it is just business. From the point of
view of the personal, the one who’s losing their bookstore, looks like an injustice because
something they love is being taken away but it is not personal. The other way to look at



                                                                                                               1/9

this is, do you have a right to have that bookstore and do you deserve to have customers,
which is to say do those customers have to show up to your business or can they go across
the street where they have a bigger selection in the giant bookstore?

Those customers have free will to go. You don’t control the customers. You can influence
with your pricing, you can influence with your selection but you can’t control the
customer’s choice. If you respect that the customer has a choice and that you’re not
entitled to a customer coming into your store you are not entitled to the business which
means you’re not entitled to the revenue, you’re not entitled or insured or guaranteed that
you’re going to be profitable and you don’t have the right to zone for miles around you to
keep competition out, you can’t control other businesses.

Then if you have the awareness that you can’t control these outside circumstances of
competition of zoning of customers’ choice if you recognize you don’t have the right to
control the things, you recognize with respect that they have a choice. Then you are not
disappointed, frustrated, and angry about the competition and the fate of your business.
In this way, then by your respect for the world you can detach emotionally from your
business when it’s time for it to go to war if it follows that fate or whenever it follows that
fate.

Let’s get one that’s a bit more personal and sometimes harder to detach from. That has to
do with our body. If something happens to our body it really feels personal like it’s
happening to us. That is a strong identification we have and if something’s happening to
our body it’s happening to me. It’s a big shift in point of view as much as we practice being
the observer to really shift out and be the observer of a body and that body is in yours.
Start yours as in you can control it all the time and that you have total dominion over it
and that it’s not you.

It’s a completely different relationship when you do that but just notice for example the
fact that you can’t control your breath completely. You can influence it but if you exhale
all your air and try to hold that or inhale and try and hold your breath, in a couple of
minutes you are going to be breathing again. There is a life force in that body, that’s
pushing it to breathe and you don’t have complete will over that life force, something as
simple as your breath, you can influence it.

The same thing is true about the death for that body. In a certain point death will come for
that body. You don’t control these outcomes. This is a sober way to live, to have this
honest acceptance of mortality. It’s not doom and gloom. No actually won’t you accept it.
There’s an incredible euphoria that comes with that perspective of like oh my God I have
this time now and I don’t have an unlimited supply so let me make the most of it. So
there’s a euphoria in that acceptance after you face what the mind perceives as doom and
gloom but I’m getting ahead of myself here.

I share a story of a client. He had a sciatic condition which I’ve had and if you know
anything about it it’s really rather quite painful. Just to sit up or walk it run shooting
pains through your leg and your back. It goes on for days and weeks and the mind really
takes an attachment to when the body is in pain and it feels like us that’s in pain. We



                                                                                                               2/9

wanted to stop and the victim part of the mind often uses that pain in the body as an
opportunity to generate a story and the story was a projection that I’m going to live the
rest of my life in this kind of pain and exaggerating the scenario that he could then fear he
was going to live in pain, the rest of his life.

And another kind of story that he was running in his mind was I don’t deserve this and we
inventoried that it went back to the days of being a kid and feeling ridiculed by other kids
and making promises to show them and making agreements with God that God’s going
take care of them and look out from in his life to make up for this because he didn’t really
deserve this, being made fun of and this victim that had made this agreement when he
was a child was there screaming out I don’t deserve this. This is an injustice. This pain in
my body is an injustice. He felt betrayed, abandoned. We should say the victim, story in
the mind was a story of betrayal and abandonment by God based on this agreement he
made as a young child, really ironic because this gentleman is an atheist but he was a little
kid and he still made agreements with God or at least that God that is in his imagination
but that God it’s in his imagination isn’t the one that’s in charge of his body.

The point is and I think I do have one here as, his sense of what he was entitled to as far as
health for his body was a basis for feeling victimized when his body wasn’t healthy. When
his body was in pain the victim story had leeway to leverage the story of injustice and
therefore really run with being unhappy emotionally about what the body was feeling
physically. This is only really something you can do as an observer of the body, to be able
to observe the story of the victim as separate from the pain of the body and to be aware of
that as separate of you as the observer. It’s a lot of awareness but when you’re able to do
that you can see that the body is in physical pain, a pain it doesn’t deserve, that didn’t do
anything wrong, nobody did anything wrong. Nobody wished that pain for that person
and yet the victim makes a story as if it’s being punished assuming it did something wrong
unnecessarily or without justification.

The victim part of the mind is using logic and reasoning in a structure of cause-and-effect.
The victim part of the mind is using an attachment to what the body should deserve, how
it should be as a basis for not getting what it wants. But in truth who said we are going to
have a body that was never going to be in pain. I don’t know that that’s a guarantee
written anywhere but the victim was using that idea of a guarantee and idea of a promise
it had in his mind, the expectation, my body should never be in pain, at least not this kind
of pain.

That attachment to that expectation of health for the body was driving an emotional story
of victimization and suffering on top of the physical pain. It might be kind of challenging
for some people to realize that you can be in physical pain and still be happy. I won’t go
into stories about it but if you review your life or you’ve seen people maybe they stumbled
they fell, they laughed about it that yet hurts but they’re so busy laughing themselves
because of a silly thing they did, big deal. So it’s possible and the reason it’s possible is if
you’re not attached to that sense of what you’re entitled to in terms of health or sensations
in your body.





                                                                                                               3/9

Let me give you another scenario of expectation for injustice that the mind creates. A
friend called up, former client and she was particularly upset. As a close family friend who
had been diagnosed with cancer and was a second or third round in this time it was throw
in the towel time. She really loved, close family friend for a lot of years and she was
battling with this whole injustice of it, he doesn’t deserve it. Good guy and she asked me
why death? That’s a fair question but if we are going to answer that question let’s put it in
a frame but put it in a reference where it can be answered with a different point of view
than the one she was in. I asked her what comes before death. Life. What comes before
life? Birth. Then why birth, why birth and life at all? But no answer for that, not a logical
one. There’s this force of nature and creation that is going on, a little bigger than logic.

Anyways she wasn’t really trying to understand why there is death, which she was really
trying to do was get out of the pain she was in of losing someone she loves. What I’m
pointing to here is with the much larger perspective you could begin to wonder why she
ever got to experience him in her life at all. There was no guarantee that he would ever be
there. There was no promise, there was no contract of getting to have him in her life for
any period of time but hidden behind her, upset at the pending loss is the assumption that
he’s supposed to be there at all and he supposed to continue to be there in the future.

She’s reacting to losing him but losing him assumes that you get to have him in the first
place. Is just so suddenly assumed and then the reaction comes when they go. What I’m
pointing to here is a kind of logic of this reason. Why is there death? Which is really
asking why is there pain? Why am I in pain? Looking for a rational basis of cause-and-
effect but it doesn’t look at the paradigm it set up by the expectation. Reasoning mind of
logic cause-and-effect, structures that assumption, he should be here, I should have this,
this is what’s fair and then when it doesn’t happen has a reaction to the belief, the
expectation that it set up. We could say we have a reaction to the belief that we set up as
expectation and because we were only looking at this in a cause-and-effect point of view
we are trapped.

We have to step back to a much larger reference frame and see the initial expectation, the
assumption paradigm that we have about life. Let’s go a little more personal still. Suppose
your husband leaves you for a younger woman, better looking and with more money or
your wife leave you for a younger man, better looking with more money. Maybe she’s
miserably unhappy and then he gets what he deserves, with more money and better
looking and miserably unhappy, let me tell you it’s not a great trade-off but this is not the
point, I digressed just for a sense of humor because it’s gotten a little heavy in here.

The point is you aren’t entitled to have them in your life. Yes that people make marriage
contracts and it’s vows for till death do us part. There is also such things as forces of life,
of course agreements can change over time. People’s interest may change. Whatever it is
there’s other forces in life than a promise that was made a year ago or 10 years ago or 30
years ago. There’s other forces in life that can change those directions and this is a real
princess attitude of entitlement of expectation, that someone will be there for the rest of
our life. Even if they aren’t stolen and I use that word stolen intentionally away by
someone else, death is going to take them eventually.




                                                                                                               4/9

Death can take him any day. Death is that great equalizer that says nothing gets a
guarantee. You don’t get to be in charge of everything. You need to get to be in charge of
your own body in your own life … There won’t be a guarantee that you’re going to be here
next week or next year or tomorrow. So what would cause us in our mind to make the
assumption that someone was stolen from us, taken from us, abandon us, when we
couldn’t even possibly know that they were going to be there to begin with but if we made
the assumption, the expectation, oh they are going to be there for us then whatever
happens that doesn’t fit that picture that that’s an injustice, our law of expectation was
broken.

Our personal law of expectation was broken but in the facts of life which is the facts of life
and death, those expectations that sense of entitlement doesn’t hold up. One of the things
that exaggerates this kind of attachment is word like my or mind. An idea or conceptual
idea of possession that it’s ours, that someone else is ours, my wife, and my husband. This
word just in use a sense of ownership that it belongs to us, that was ever ours to have in
the first place as in ours to keep, ours to expect to be there. Personal life may be ours to
love, share with, enjoy, appreciate, play with, argue with but they aren’t ours.

We can express our love to them but they are not ours. They just like us are visiting here
for a short time and whether they go off to be with someone else or whether they go on
their journey into the next world, however you want to describe that, ours is a choice to
cling to them and take them for granted where ours is a choice to appreciate them for the
time we have with them and appreciate our body for the time we have with it, whether it’s
in pain or it’s in health. What I’m talking about here, what I’m pointing to here is a
profound level of acceptance, detachment and a lot of people think of detachment as
disassociating from not caring about but that’s a very far from the truth.

This kind of detachment that comes with awareness of no expectations, no entitlement
actually deepens our appreciation, deepens our respect and can open us up to love, even
more love unconditionally with no expectations, no need to control and make it fit our
expectations, love people the way they are and whatever choices they make. Then this
kind of detachment that’s in the frame of understanding life and death deepens our
reverence for everything in life. The dangers to look out in these kinds of expectations are
the ones where we look to possess, where we look to hold and keep, attached to in a way
that something’s ours and that we can control it. It’s similar to an image of perfection that
the judge generates but more specifically it’s close to the Princess archetype and it’s a
sense of entitlement and expectation.

The reaction to not having that expectation met, that sense of entitlement can be a sense
of justice or fairness how the world should be, how people should treat us, not having that
met makes it open season for the victim to tell the story and make it believable. When you
expect your body to have no pain than having pain is unfair, it’s not right, victim material.
If you expect to live the life without death interfering, without changes you don’t want
than anything that doesn’t fit your picture and expectation is a disturbance. It’s not right,
not fair, you don’t deserve it and its prime material for the victim story to feel victimized





                                                                                                               5/9

about life and the way life changes but the predecessor to all those victim stories are the
sense of entitlement’s and idea of fairness and idea of what’s right, not to set up for the
victimization.

I’m not inviting you to give up on creating your life the way you want it. Go intended and
take action. I’m just inviting you to give up your attachments and expectations and sense
of entitlement that creates emotional suffering. One of the assignments I’ve given clients
before is to take death in this way as their teacher and do things like take a piece of paper,
a blank white sheet of paper and put on it everything you expect and you soon will be in
your life tomorrow or next week and then put that on the fridge and if you’re planning a
vacation for the summer or you buy tickets to go see your family during the holidays,
you’re expecting to get there, you can put that on your sheet of paper but then to
understand everything that you put on that sheet of paper and you assume you’re going to
have it is something you’re taking for granted. It’s a point of view, there’s nothing wrong
with doing it but let me propose to you the alternative.

That you leave your sheet of paper white, which is to clean your mind of expectations. In a
sense that you are entitled or deserve anything and then what ever shows up in your life is
a gift. You are still going to plan and you’re still going to take action. You are still going to
buy the plane tickets and get on that plane and go see your family. You are going to plan
your vacation and you’re going to enjoy it so your plans and your intent is still there, it’s
just without the expectation, the assumption and the taking it for granted portion.

Your next breath, next heartbeat is a gift, or you can take it for granted depending on your
point of view. The people in your life are a gift every moment you get to see them or you
can take them for granted depending on your point of view. Whatever you have in your
life, whatever comforts and health you have in your life is a gift or its material for the
victim part of the mind to feel abused because it doesn’t fit its imaginary picture of
expectation. These are just choices in your point of view and point of interpretation. What
assumptions are you going to make, meaning what expectations you can make? Not right,
not wrong just different experiences of life depending on the point of view in the
interpretation you adopt. So your mission if you choose to accept it is to hunt down the
fuel for all these victimization stories.

You might call this process the last of victimization it’s hunting down the last bits of them
and they really begin the expectation portion of the mind in places where we project a
sense of entitlement, then the specific keywords were hunting for here are those kinds of
words that we use in our dialogue, that relate to a sense of entitlement. You can also hunt
your victim stories and you can backtrack to what expectations proceeded that victim
story, what was the expectation that didn’t get met? But in hunting the words, keywords
to look for are words like deserve or deserving. I didn’t deserve that. If someone takes my
business away they come and they shoot me you I didn’t deserve it but I didn’t deserve to
have a body either. Nowhere is that in the contract. A sense of justice that’s the keyword
set up for victimization, fairness, mine for what is right.





                                                                                                               6/9

These are the kinds of attachments to entitlement. It’s not right that they took that from
me, he didn’t do right by me, that was mine, I want justice. These are crying out victim
stories, needs the keywords. That isn’t fair, what they did to them wasn’t fair, this is a
victim story, it goes with injustice, goes with feeling abused and betrayed. Why? Because
we’re attached to it a sense of some other picture that we feel entitled to, some other
picture that only exist in imagination, that doesn’t take into account the facts of life and
death and that the world is a big place. And when I say the world’s a big place, I want to
cover two things about this whole entitlement and fairness and justice.

Growing up in the U.S there are certain rights that I’m given by the Constitution and the
mind can assume that yes those rights I should have but you know what, if I grew up in a
different country I don’t have those same rights. I don’t have prevention against search
and seizure. I don’t have free speech. I’m not free to choose my faith and spiritual
practice. If I go to a country like that, am I abused? No, it’s just that they have their own
rules and I wouldn’t expect that I could live by the rules in this country, in another
country. It’s like a squirrel expecting to go live in a coyote stand. The coyotes are going to
have a problem with that. It’s just nature. Could it be different in a world? Yes. But is it?
No then I’m not expecting it to be any different today. I will intend for it to change but I
will not expect it to be any different.

In the realm of conscious creation one of the ways that I’ve seen people use this idea of
manifesting a new life, even seen them use that to abuse themselves. One woman studying
this whole how to create your life, focus your thoughts and it’ll manifest come stuff, runs
around a lot these new thought churches, and she c as you can figure out why the stuff
that she wanted to create wasn’t manifesting. She’s told that she’s is a very powerful
person and that she can create whatever she wants but what she wants to create doesn’t
happen and then she feels like she’s a failure because her expectations aren’t being met.
She’s not the great creator that she believes she should be, she expects to be. It’s kind of…
in dynamic where these spiritual teachings were intended to empower people, by teaching
them that they are powerful creators but when the stuff didn’t get created these people
were feeling like failures, they weren’t getting the results that they expected and her judge
beat up on her victim that she must be a failure, she’s doing it wrong.

There’s some things that we can create and there are also some limitations.You have to
understand the process. If I want to go play in the NBA no matter how hard I work at this
point, no matter how much I believe is not going to happen. This body is just not going to
do it. In those powerful acts as magic of intent to create our own reality but say that I
want to heal my body, well let’s say I intended, I believe it’s possible, I go for it but it
doesn’t happen. Understanding that field of creating, that field of magic is not just about
thinking that it’s possible and believing that it’s possible I can heal my body, that art of
being a healer may take some skill as well.

If you go study healing and how to heal through faith, now you have a better chance,
because you will master the skill, but just expecting it, you know that’s like me watching
someone do heart surgery and saving a person’s life and going oh I can save a person’s
life. Well the truth is I can’t save a person’s life, but that doesn’t mean I should just go do




                                                                                                               7/9

open-heart surgery. No, I can save a person’s life with open-heart surgery but I better go
study how first and that may take a little while and then put me in the operating room,
now I can save a life.

Well, the same is true in a way for that science of healing, that mastery of healing with
intent and faith, there are people who are able to do it and it’s possible but don’t read a
book and expect that you know how to be a healer. Don’t be introduced to the idea and
expect that people are going to be healed because you think they will be. No there is a
mastery of intent to shift people’s bodies that way and its best achieved if you practice.
This has an art, a skill, a science to it. What I’m pointing to you here is misplaced
expectations because these incredible things about creating your life consciously and
creating what you want are possible but they also require skills and those skills need to be
developed and nurtured and honed than expecting yourself to manifest perfectly what you
want to. Just because you thought about it, it doesn’t mean you have the skill, then
expecting the outcome without learning the art that may be involved is a misplaced
expectation that can cause you to abuse yourself or be victimized by the thoughts in your
mind.

So is there justice? It depends in your point of view. If were out in the woods and we are
watching the bunnies play, eating the grass, looks like beautiful justice and then the
coyote comes and runs in and eats the rabbit. From the point of view of the coyote that
rabbit is a blessing. If you wanted to make an interpretation that way it had a mind to do
so from the point of view of the rabbit if it had a victim, my interpretation it might feel
victimized and say it’s injustice, unfair, but then what of the grasses point of view, they
look at the coyote that saved it from the rabbit that was chewing on it. Feeling victimized
is a point of view and what precedes it is a sense of expectation entitlement.

Your mission if you choose to is to hunt down where we play the victim and behind that
story of abuse, disrespect what have you? Look for the expectations of entitlement. I don’t
deserve to be treated that way. Where are the keywords of deserved justice? Fairness,
right, what’s mine. Put that in the context of death, put that in the context of being born in
a different country, in a third world country and consider what you really have the rights
to, what you’re guaranteed.

Look at a blank sheet of paper and tell me for sure what you know you’re going to have
tomorrow and then decide if you want to interpret from the victim and entitlement point
of view. In one path you get to be happy and grateful and be in awe of this world of
creation and the opportunity to create and express experience. In the other path you get
to expect, feel entitled, cling to and suffering. There are many paths more than these two.
There are billions of choices we can make. Create your own. Just understand and be
aware there’s emotional consequences for every interpretation or belief that you make.

Happy hunting to ferret out the victim stories and beliefs and sense of entitlement. This is
Gary van Warmerdam from a pathway to happiness about the facts of life and that you
have the opportunity to create and express but you have no guarantees and that makes
things kind of exciting. Thank you.

Developing Gratitude

    pathwaytohappiness.com/blog/developing-an-attitude-of-gratitude

                                                                              December 9, 2006

One of the free exercises in my Self Mastery Introductory Course is about gratitude. You
will find gratitude is a common element of happiness. All the experts recommend various
ways to practice it. When people take on this practice of gratitude they usually do it for
several days and then it tails off. Other distractions get a hold of their attention and
gratitude, which is a form of happiness, loses priority to habit.

Changing habits can take some time. But changing your attitude to one of gratitude
usually has a hidden core belief that creates an obstacle of resistance. That hidden core
belief often prevents us from living in gratitude. Eliminating this core belief can help
make the change faster. It is a paradigm of the mind that filters the way we see the world.
It filters our perception in such a way that the feeling of gratitude becomes nearly
impossible to sustain.

What is that core belief that we can’t see that filters our view of the world? It is simply that
we assume the people we love and the things we care about will be there next week. We
are so familiar with our things like the comforts of running water, a warm place to stay,
our eyesight, and the people we love, that we take them for granted.

Without awareness, we assume that not much will change between now and tomorrow.
We live by the unseen assumption that not much will change in a month or a year. We
look forward with optimism that we won’t lose what we have. We assume we will just gain
more over time as if our lives were accumulating interest between now and when we pass
on. We don’t acknowledge that the health of our bodies, our time, and the people we love
are not gaining any time. You and the people you love are in the process of passing away
from this world. When we don’t acknowledge that the landscape of our life is changing,
and sometimes it changes fast, we end up not appreciating the time we have.

Our capacity and feeling of gratitude are inversely related to how much we take for
granted. Those that walk around their day filled with gratitude take little to nothing for
granted. People that live in an unseen belief paradigm that everything and everyone they
care about will be there next week have a difficult time attaining a deep feeling of
gratitude or sustaining the emotion for very long. For these people, gratitude may only
come immediately following fear filled close calls of tragedy.

Core beliefs are often bubbles of perception. When those bubbles break, either we are
angry that we have lost our illusion, or we are grateful to finally embrace life in a very
intimate and precious way.

    “There are only two ways to live your life. One is as though nothing is a miracle, the other
      is as if everything is. I believe in the latter.”
     Albert Einstein.




                                                                                                               1/2

I will post a self-awareness exercise in the Gratitude section of the member’s area
that will help chip away at this blinding core belief. You will need to signup to access this
audio.





                                                                                                               2/2

Getting Your Needs Met Without Being Needy

   pathwaytohappiness.com/blog/needs-and-needy

                                                                                    March 3, 2015

Getting Your Needs Met Without Being Needy

Having needs is not the same as being needy. No man is an island. And neither is a
woman. We all have needs, but we don’t have to go about getting them met in a needy
way. Most days as an adult, we can take care of many, but not all of our needs. We
probably didn’t build our own house, get the water to run indoors, or farm our own food.
Yet growing up into adulthood we acquire the belief that we should be able to take care of
everything our self. As a result we ignore the reality of our interdependence. We might
even believe the illusion that we can or do take care of all our own needs. This kind of
false belief is likely to lead to unhappiness in areas of your life.

If you are trying to project that positive self-image, which is often done in relationships,
expressing needs looks like a stain of weakness on the success image we try to convey.
 Indeed, today’s western economy makes it possible to meet all our own physical survival
needs by ourselves. We can earn enough money to provide water, food, shelter, and rest in
comfortable fashion. At first glance, it looks like all our needs are met. However, in order
to be happy and fulfilled, we need to have other experiences other than survival and that
requires we meet other needs in ways we might not have considered.

We are complex beings and therefore have different kinds of needs.

Emotionally, we have a need to love and be loved. These can take many forms like
respect, appreciation, compassion, laughter, or other emotions. At other times it will be
necessary to be in touch with emotions like grief, sadness, anger, or remorse so they can
be processed and released. Without allowing ourselves to experience these we repress
them and cut ourselves off from all emotions, not just the unpleasant ones. Suppressing
emotions keeps us from being fully present and feeling alive in the moment.

For a relationship to be satisfying it will need to have mutual support, affection, sexual
satisfaction, play, fun. It will also need to be emotionally safe with feelings of connection,
respect, and appreciation. You don’t need these things to survive, but you will need them
to be happy in a relationship. A client, Jason, was finding that he wasn’t getting the kind
of intimate time he wanted with his girlfriend, Anna. He asked her if they could spend
time during the week with their phones off, just paying attention and listening to each
other. He also asked for more time being affectionate, cuddling, and relaxing together.
Anna laughed it off, saying Jason was just being needy. In Anna’s world of beliefs, which
made her successful in a corporate environment, “needy” meant being pathetic, weak.
Not long after, Jason figured out that by having what he asked for dismiss and judged by
Anna, that he didn’t really need Anna.





                                                                                                               1/3

Our mind has its own needs. The mind needs to be creative and dream. It needs to be
exercised, inspired, and at times spontaneous so it doesn’t suffer in boredom. At times it
will be good to be challenged so we stretch, grow, and learn. We also may have a need for
our mind to be quiet and peaceful at times so we can relax and rest.

The aspect of our Spirit has a need for a connection to something bigger, whether you call
it the cosmos, nature, or something more divine. The path to this connection will feel like
a need for freedom, adventure, or at times isolation. The yearning for a connection to a
greater consciousness can cause us to ache. If we do not seek out this connection and
activity, whether it be through something inward like meditation, or outward like
camping or church, we will ache in an unfulfilled way.

At a soul level we may need a connection to a community, the earth, or our fellow human
beings. Sometimes this need is satisfied with a sense of purpose or meaningful work.
Sometimes this need gest satisfied with gardening. If you don’t’ find this need met with
your job or hobby, then you will have to pursue volunteering. Perhaps this need of the
soul is met with a contribution to a community, or harmony with others at church.

Judging Our Needs

If our ego is so intent on not needing anything from anybody, then we are minimizing the
importance of our happiness in the areas that nurture our emotions, relationships, spirit,
and soul. Our ego will point to a hard outer shell and feel good about being strong and
independent. At the same time the voice in our head is busy telling us that these feelings
on the inside are not important and that we are being pathetic and weak for having them.
This kind of self judgment will create an emotional reaction of insecurity or shame that
will need to be dissolved. Sometimes this kind of self-judgment gets compounded with a
fear that others will think of us as needy because we have these feelings. It is these kinds
of contradicting stories in our head, one that says we are independent, and a contrary one
that says we are weak, that are clues that we are out of our integrity. Not only are we
isolating ourselves from others in ways that we could connect, we are not satisfying these
needs that are essential to be happy.

Judging these needs/desires as weak, pathetic, or dismissing them represses them. When
the needs of our soul, spirit, and emotional body are repressed we don’t take actions to
have them met and parts of our being continue to hunger and ache. The outcome of this
lack of action is that we won’t have what we need to love, feel loved, fulfilled, and happy.
In this case we might not be allowing our self to feel our real needs enough.

Over a long time of repressing these very real needs our pain grows and we feel victimized
and then become frustrated, agitated, and angry. At this point real needs fester into a
neediness driven by the victim aspect of the ego feels and we might desperate. This is
when we become the kind of needy other people don’t want to be around.

Good Needs and Dreaded “Being Needy”





                                                                                                               2/3

As we look at having our needs met, we need to have an awareness of the difference
between real needs, and victim needs of the ego or we will venture into suffering at the
other extreme. A clue that you are crossing the line from good needs into destructive
needs are when your wants become feelings of desperation, fear, or insecurity. Another
sign is if we are calculating our gestures in an effort to be covert and get what we want. If
we are not being honest with our partner, then we probably aren’t being entirely honest
with our self. The Victim aspect of the ego only looks to others, and not to our self to
make us feel better. And when feelings persist, or false expectations aren’t met, the victim
aspect blames others for the disappointment, toxic emotions, and circumstances.

If you are hurt or blaming, then you are past the ego’s Victim aspect of needy and have
possibly turned angry about it. If you find yourself making ultimatums or demanding
someone do something for you, or you believe they are the only one that can meet your
need then you have crossed the line as well. If your needs aren’t being met and you
respond with emotional punishments like disappointment, judgment, resentment, or
frustration, then you are engaged in an unhealthy neediness. Emotional punishment is
not a good long term strategy for satisfying needs. Heck, it’s not even a good short term
strategy. If we are trying to get our needs met in this way, people around us will withdraw,
and we will be further away from the satisfaction and happiness we desire.

A quick question to ask yourself is whether you are operating above or below the line of
feeling neutral. If your need involves getting out of an emotional pit like of fear, despair,
or insecurity then you are likely operating from the Victim part of the ego. If your need
involves feeling more love, happiness, appreciation, or connection, then you are probably
working on good needs that involve healthy positive interactions with others. The long
term answer is awareness of several aspects; what your needs are, when they are victim
ego driven, how you ask, and whether the people around you can or will provide for what
you ask.

We are complex beings requiring only a few physical things to survive, but many other
intangible things in order to flourish and be happy. Holding rigidly to the belief of “not
being needy” causes us to blur the line between material and everything else. We think of
food, water, and shelter as needs, and everything else as wants. We tell ourselves we can
do without “wants” and “desires” because we don’t need them. However, these “wants”
and “desires” are what we need in order to be happy and fulfilled. Maybe part of the
problem here is that we don’t think of being happy or feeling fulfilled, as important in our
life to have the status of a need. How important is being happy to you? Until it is
important, we dismiss our wants and desires and live a life unfulfilled and unhappy. You
don’t have to consider satisfying wants and desires necessary for survival, but they are
essential needs for spiritual, emotional well-being, and happiness.





                                                                                                               3/3

Help Asking For What You Want

   pathwaytohappiness.com/blog/help-asking-for-what-you-want

                                                                                    March 8, 2016

Asking for what you want might seem like a simple thing, but it isn’t. It is a complex
process of noticing your desires, eliminating the selfish and unreasonable, feeling worthy
of having, feeling safe that you won’t be judged or rejected, finding the time and space to
be heard in our busy lives and competition for attention, and then phasing our request in
a way that they hear and feel how important it is to us. If you are at work all this might get
pushed aside because your priority is to take care of your boss’s needs, clients needs, and
co-workers so that you can keep your job and take care of your financial needs. If you are
a parent taking care of kids you might be so busy that you don’t have time to notice your
own needs. When there is a break in the action and you have time to slow down, maybe all
you notice is that you are too tired to want anything else. That is your sign that you need
time to rest by the way.

This isn’t the complete list of how to become aware of what you want and how to ask for
it, but it should help.

Know that wanting something for yourself isn’t selfish.

When you believe that asking for something that you want is selfish, you don’t allow
yourself to even ask. Often, when sub-consciously you feel it would be selfish, you might
even repress the desire for it, or quickly dismiss it mentally when the desire comes up.
This kind of self-negation can stop your request from getting out of your mouth, or distort
the way you ask so it is no longer clear that it is important to you.

Asking for what you want doesn’t mean you are needy.

Having desires, wants, and needs is a natural part of the human experience. We have a
desire for water when we are thirsty, and food when we are hungry. These aren’t the only
wants, needs, and desires we have as normal human beings. Other wants and needs that
are natural are for emotional connection, support, time for our self, freedom, empathy,
compassion, affection, understanding, sex, creativity, physical exercise, and to express our
own authentic voice. When we don’t have these needs met we get restless, frustrated, or
possibly depressed. Having wants and desires is natural. It doesn’t mean we are weak or
petty. It means we are human. Meeting our wants and needs is what helps us feel
satisfied and fulfilled.

Recognize that it is not the other person’s responsibility to provide what we
ask for.

It is their choice. They can say no, or negotiate for something in between. If you demand
or try to obligate another person to meet your needs and wants you may be interfering
with their freedom of choice. People we ask have their own needs and when we obligate
others we are not respecting what they need and want. If you ask someone and they say



                                                                                                               1/2

no, that has to be okay. If you become angry, annoyed, frustrated, or withdraw, then that
kind of emotional punishment is a sign that you are not respecting their choices. It is okay
if they say no. You don’t have to have all your needs and wants met by one person.

Tell the person you are asking how you feel and what it means to have what
you are asking for.

If you are asking for some time alone your partner might think you don’t like him and
reject himself with the lack of information. If you inform him that your time alone is how
you nurture your soul and spirit so you can be more of yourself and better with him, then
he is more likely to say yes, and feel good about it.

Always express appreciation.

If someone provides something you asked for then make sure they know you appreciate it.
A big hug with your words makes more of an impact. Getting appreciation from people,
particularly our partner is one way we get emotionally nourished in relationships. When
people are recognized and appreciated for what they do they feel better about doing it and
want to do it more. That means you will both be getting more of what you want.

Be reasonable and negotiate.

You might want that 2 week vacation to the Greek Islands this summer and you might not
feel it is selfish. That’s good. But your partner might not want to empty the bank account
to give it to you. That doesn’t mean he doesn’t love you. It just might be interfering with
his need to provide for the family long term. Listen to what your partner’s needs are and
how they can be met. Asking questions and listening to what your partner’s needs helps
them get their needs met. Sometimes they might not be able to articulate exactly what
their needs are. Those needs might seem like random thoughts and uncomfortable
feelings at first. Asking questions and providing a space to listen will help them identify
and articulate what they want and need. When you can help them get what they need in
the negotiation then they are more likely to give you what you want as well. You might
also discover that what you really wanted was a romantic dream getaway to a beach
island. You might find that the middle ground that gets both your real needs and wants
met is an island in the Florida Keys for a few days.

For Better Self Awareness so you can identify what you want more clearly, and clearly ask
for what you want, check out Gary van Warmerdam’s Self Mastery Course.





                                                                                                               2/2
